valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 27 Nov 2026. (1) Business: two parts, weighted by H1 FY2027 segment results (Interim to 30 Sep 2026, PDF p. 9): financial services (hire purchase inside Singer plus Singer Finance (Lanka) PLC) Rs 3.86bn of Rs 8.96bn = 43%; retail and manufacturing of durables (home appliances, digital, electronics, furniture, sewing, automobiles) 57%. (2) Damodaran's emerging-markets dataset (betaEmerg) could NOT be opened: his site is blocked by this run's network settings. Stand-ins from web-search extracts: Retail (Special Lines) global unlevered, cash-corrected 0.90 (date not shown in the extract); Financial Svcs. (Non-bank & Insurance) levered 0.97 (January 2026, as used for HNB Finance and Central Finance on this site). (3) Retail relevered with the company's own net debt (Singer PLC without Singer Finance) of Rs 49.65bn at 30 Sep 2026 (loans 6.124 + 41.776, overdrafts 3.143, leases 4.058 + 1.150, less cash 2.128 and bank deposits 4.474; Interim to 30 Sep 2026, PDF p. 4) ÷ market value Rs 84.65bn (1,167.6mn shares × Rs 72.50, CSE close 27 Nov 2026) = 0.59, at the 30% statutory rate: 0.90 × (1 + 0.70 × 0.59) = 1.27. The finance part uses the sector's levered beta without relevering, as the brief says for finance companies. Weighted: 0.57 × 1.27 + 0.43 × 0.97 = 1.14. (4) Local 5-year betas: only one found, StockAnalysis 0.41 (5Y, undated web-search extract); TradingView gives 1-year betas only (0.90–1.94, ignored). The share trades thinly (10.94% public holding), so local betas are set aside anyway. (5) 1.14. (6) Within 0.3–2. (7) Into the formula by scripts/reinvestment.py. (8) Shown as the Required return tile. Provisional: refresh in January 2027 with Damodaran's emerging-markets file.

valuationInputs.name: Cost of equity
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (27 Nov 2026): 8.24% + 1.14 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 20.0%, ±1.5 points. Replaces the hand-set 21 / 19 / 17.5% of 8 Nov.

valuationInputs.name: WACC
valuationInputs.reason: Most of the group's debt funds customer credit (hire purchase and Singer Finance loans), so it is treated like a finance company: equity methods at the cost of equity, no whole-company DCF and no WACC.

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 4% / 8% / 12% (dividend growth for five years); supported 28.3% (share of profit kept 70.7% × ROE 40.0%, FY 2026). All within 2 pts.
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py on FY 2026. At the base long-run ROE of 24% and a 30% payout the supported rate would still be about 17%, so the assumptions are well inside it. Long-run 6% at 24% ROE needs a quarter of profit kept (stable payout 75%).

valuationInputs.name: Long-run ROE
valuationInputs.reason: Return on average net assets as printed: 28, 35, 1, −1, 29, 40% for FY2021–26 (decade table, pp. 303–304), average about 22%; 10-year average about 18%; 40.3% on the last 12 months (derived.py). Recent returns rest on net debt of 4x equity and a consumer boom; two of the last six years were close to zero. Used for P/B, justified P/E, residual income and the dividend model.

valuationInputs.name: Long-term growth
valuationInputs.reason: Below the 12.24% bond yield; roughly nominal economic growth.

valuationInputs.name: EPS to March 2027
valuationInputs.reason: H1 EPS Rs 3.00 (Interim to 30 Sep 2026, PDF p. 2). Second half Rs 2.80 / 3.60 / 4.20 against Rs 3.78 last year (6.29 − 2.51): the September quarter fell 6% (Rs 1.16 vs 1.23) as finance costs nearly doubled. Base is 2.7% below the Rs 6.78 twelve-month run-rate.

valuationInputs.name: Dividend to March 2027
valuationInputs.reason: Rs 0.84 declared for the first half (0.50 + 0.34); Rs 1.84 for 2025/26 (a 29% payout, including a Rs 0.85 fourth interim). About 28–29% of the EPS assumed.

valuationInputs.name: Dividend growth
valuationInputs.reason: Below the supported growth (Growth check); then the stable payout 1 − g ÷ ROE.

valuationInputs.name: Residual income path
valuationInputs.value: ROE from 40.3% now to 18% / 24% / 30% over five years; payout 30%
valuationInputs.reason: Starting ROE is the last 12 months (derived.py ttm.roe). Five years rather than ten because Singer's ROE has collapsed to about zero twice since 2019 (FY2019–20 and FY2023–24). Payout 29% in 2025/26.

valuationInputs.name: Methods used
valuationInputs.value: Justified P/B, P/E (justified), residual income, dividend model
valuationInputs.reason: Equity methods, as for a finance company: a cash-flow DCF doesn't work while operating cash flow is negative every year because customer credit grows (−Rs 41.6bn in 2025/26). Inputs saved as modelInputs in data/SINS.N0000.json; values from scripts/valuation.py.

openQuestions: Q3 results (to December 2026, the festive quarter, due by mid-February 2027): does profit grow again, or fall for a second quarter?
Do finance costs keep rising faster than revenue (+74% against +30% in H1)?
Bad-debt charges rose 53% in H1: are they rising faster than customer credit (+Rs 12.1bn)?
Does net debt (incl. leases) rise above 4.5x owners' equity (4.1x at Sep 2026)?
Which section does the next report put Singer Finance's deposit increase in (operating in H1, financing in the annual and June reports)?
Court of Appeal ruling on the Rs 1.19bn deemed-VAT case, and the 2017–2022 VAT and income tax appeals (no provisions).
Cost and timing of the furniture factory purchase; refresh the beta with Damodaran's emerging-markets file in January 2027.

changeLog.summary: Six-month results: revenue up 30%, profit up 20%, but September-quarter profit fell 6% as finance costs doubled; net debt 3.5x equity. Lowered EPS for the year to March 2027 (base 7.6 → 6.6) and the starting ROE in residual income. Fair value Rs 45.0 → 42.3. Category 3 unchanged (1 of 4 tests).

Requested from Telegram (/redo SINS.N0000 full). Research record rebuilt from the downloaded annual report 2025/26 and the interims to June and September 2026, on the report-figures-only format (printed lines with pages, comparative columns as their own periods, FY2021–24 from the decade table); the old worked-out netDebt and netDebtToEquity entries were replaced by borrowings, lease and cash lines. New sections: required return from a beta of 1.14 (provisional; Damodaran stand-ins from web search, his site was blocked), management and plans, shareholders. Methods now justified P/B, justified P/E, residual income (five-year fade) and the dividend model at a 20.0% cost of equity (was a hand-set 19% and chosen P/E of 7/9/11x). Fair value Rs 42.30 → 30.22, mainly from the justified P/E (5.4x base) and the higher required return. Business tests 1 of 4, category 3 unchanged. Uncertain: no 3 local 5-year betas (thin trading); the H1 report puts customer deposits in operating cash flow, unlike the annual and June reports; workingCapitalChange left null (no printed subtotal).
